items.title: Henry A. "Hank" Kmen Interview, 1963-02-13
items.q: I remember that band so well coming on the radio at noontime when I was a kid still in school... I've never seen reference one to that any place.

ctx.x: That's funny, I don't remember anything about him at all.

Well, we've talked about this at other times, Nick, and it really doesn't belong here, but somebody, someday, ought to dig into the big bands in America too. That whole era of bands before it's lost completely. You remember I often mention to you my favorite band up there, the Lonely Acres Band, and young Chinese Paul Tremaine and his Lonely Acres Band. I've never seen reference one to that any place. And I remember that band so well coming on the radio at noontime when I was a kid still in school, and playing…

Swinging them all. Did you ever know a fellow named Teddy Brewer, he later called himself Teddy Martin, he played Albert System clarinet on Bourbon Street, a non-human about 1950, I forget what happened to him. Fudd was playing piano with him some it seems to me, and a guy who played valve trombone, he told me something about Paul Tremaine.
